sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the difference between the matzah commanded before midnight and the matzah eaten after midnight at the Exodus, based on the spelling "matzah" with and without a vav.

translations.translation: "This matzah that we eat, for what reason? Because the dough of our forefathers did not have time to become leavened until the King of Kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself to them and redeemed them."
And it is explained in the discourses of our Nesi'im,
that this statement—that the reason for eating matzah on Pesach is because it did not have time to become leavened—
[is made] even though the commandment to eat matzah was before this,
for regarding the commandment to eat matzah it is written,
"In the evening you shall eat matzos,"
[where] "matzos" is spelled deficiently, without a vav,
and in the verse, "And they baked the dough which they brought out of Egypt into unleavened cakes, etc.,"
it is written "matzos" plene, with a vav.
For the commandment to eat matzah is before midnight,
and since before midnight they were still in Egypt,
before the King of Kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself to them,
therefore regarding this matzah it is written "matzos" deficiently, without a vav,
in contrast to the verse, "And they baked the dough which they brought out of Egypt into unleavened cakes, etc.," which speaks of the matzah they baked
(and ate)
after they left Egypt
("the dough which they brought out of Egypt")
which was after midnight,
after the King of Kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself to them and redeemed them,
therefore regarding this matzah it is written "matzos" plene, with a vav.
And this is also why regarding the matzah before midnight it is written,
"And you shall guard the matzos,"
that it requires guarding so that it does not become leavened,
whereas regarding the matzah after midnight it is written, "And they baked the dough... into unleavened cakes, for it had not leavened,"
meaning that by itself it did not become leavened,
for the matzah after midnight is of the level of "matzos" plene, with a vav,
the revelation of the King of Kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, revealing Himself to them,
and therefore it does not require guarding from leavening.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that after the Giving of the Torah, the matzah eaten on Pesach night before midnight is on the level of "matzos" plene, incorporating the revelation of the Exodus.

translations.translation: Now, this distinction between before midnight and after midnight existed only in the first Pesach,
before the Giving of the Torah.
However, after the Giving of the Torah,
even though the matzah eaten on the night of Pesach is before midnight,
it is of the level of "matzos" plene, with a vav,
for it contains
(also)
the elevation of the revelation of the King of Kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, revealing Himself to them.
And this is what is said in the Haggadah: "This matzah that we eat, for what reason? Because it did not have time... to become leavened"
(meaning that by itself it did not become leavened)
"until the King of Kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself to them and redeemed them."
